title: Reduced cartesian compactification of a finite etale cover
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a reduced separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting, def-pc-reduced-scheme], $j:U\to X$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and $v:V\to U$ finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. There exist a reduced scheme $Y$, a finite $p:Y\to X$, and an open immersion $a:V\to Y$, such that $f\circ p$ makes $Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-curve of dimension at most one and the square $(a,v,p,j)$ is cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

proof.text: The curve morphism f makes X locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Therefore j is quasi-compact, and v followed by j is separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type and locally quasi-finite. Apply Scheme.Hom.exists_isOpenImmersion_isFinite_of_locallyQuasiFinite to obtain i : V -> T open and quasi-compact and q : T -> X finite with i followed by q = v followed by j.

U is reduced since it is open in X; V is reduced by isReduced_of_etale. Take Y = i.image, a = i.toImage, p = i.imageι followed by q. The factor map a is a quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dominant open immersion. Mathlib IsSchemeTheoreticallyDominant.isReduced gives reducedness of Y (inject its section rings into the reduced section rings of V). The closed immersion i.imageι is finite, so p is finite, and composition with f is separated and of finite type.

The finite morphism p has discrete fibres and identifies no distinct specializing points: use the proved upstream Scheme.Hom.eq_of_specializes_of_apply_eq. Apply the proved topologicalKrullDim_le_of_continuous to obtain dim Y <= dim X <= 1. Together with separatedness and finite type this gives IsCurve (p followed by f). This replaces the planned affine integral-incomparability calculation by the existing quasi-finite topological comparison.

Let b : V -> Y times_X U be the pullback lift of a and v. Its composite with the first projection is a, and that projection is open, so b is an open immersion. Its composite with the second projection is the finite map v; the second projection is finite and thus separated, so IsFinite.of_comp makes b finite. Hence its range is closed. The inverse image under the first projection of range a equals range b, by injectivity of that open projection. Since range a is dense in Y, the open-map preimage-closure inclusion makes range b dense in the pullback. Closedness then makes b surjective. The surjective open immersion b is an isomorphism. IsPullback.of_iso_pullback gives the requested square. This argument uses no nonemptiness assumptions and includes the empty cover.

proof_origin: Stacks Project 03SD compactification paragraph and 05K0; formal proof by F3 using the scheme-theoretic image and the existing quasi-finite dimension comparison. The pullback comparison is proved open, finite and surjective in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_reduced_cartesian_finite_cover_compactification
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {X U V : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] [IsReduced X]
    (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] (v : V ⟶ U) [IsFinite v] [Etale v] :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y ⟶ X) (a : V ⟶ Y),
      IsFinite p ∧ IsCurve (p ≫ f) ∧ IsReduced Y ∧ IsOpenImmersion a ∧
        IsPullback a v p j
